1	# Task 2: forest of 10,000 instances
2	
3	Build a scene with Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. A ground plane and exactly 10,000 scattered objects drawn with instancing (not 10,000 separate meshes): 8,000 trees (a trunk and a canopy, each instanced) and 2,000 rocks.
7	2. Placement is deterministic from a fixed seed (same forest every load), no overlaps needed.
8	3. Per-instance colour variation (canopies and rocks do not all share one colour).
9	4. One directional light that casts shadows, and exponential fog.
10	5. The camera slowly orbits the forest and the whole scene is visible.
11	
12	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
13	
14	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
15	
16	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
17	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
18	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
19	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
20	- When you are done, call `finish`.
21

#1 [docs/agents/first-screen-cheatsheet.md :: Rules] score 26.5
## Rules
- `createAuraApp` owns renderer, resize and loop: write none. Per frame `app.onFrame((f) => ...)` (`f.dt` seconds); end with `await app.ready()`; set window flags after it (`declare global { interface Window { __FLAG__?: boolean } }`).
- Vectors `[x, y, z]`, colours CSS strings. Primitives are unit shapes scaled by `size` (`sphere` size = diameter, `plane` `[w, 1, d]` lies in XZ): `primitives.box|sphere|plane|cylinder|capsule|cone|torus`. Node chain: `.position(x, y, z)`, `.scale([x, y, z])`, `.rotate(x, y, z)`.
- Animate later: `.runtime({ id, mutable: true })` then `app.nodes.require(id).setPosition(x, y, z)` / `.setRotation(x, y, z)`; light `.setLight?.({ intensity, color })`; shader `.setUniform?.(name, v)`.
- Instance `colors` multiply the material colour: use base `#ffffff`. Dark frame: add `environments.neutral({ intensity: 0.5, background: false })` or a hemisphere light.
- Camera `camera.orbit({ ..., autoRotate: radPerSec })` orbits its target slowly; never `app.camera`.

I'm setting up the exp mode scene with an orbiting camera, large shadow coverage, and a delayed ready flag after a couple of animation frames, then laying out the scattered rocks and duplicated tree instance groups across a 75-unit radius.
The rendering contract is clear: the engine owns the loop, continuously rendering via requestAnimationFrame.

input.summary: I wrote src/main.ts, which builds the forest scene. It passes typecheck. I did not run `vite build` or open it in a browser, so I haven't seen it render. The scene has a 260×260 ground plane and 10,000 instanced objects in three draws: 8,000 trunks, 8,000 cone canopies and 2,000 rocks. Placement comes from a seeded LCG, so the forest is the same on every load. Canopies and rocks get per-instance HSL colours, and trunks share one brown. There is one shadow-casting directional light plus a hemisphere light, and exponential fog (`mode: "exp"`, density 0.0045). The camera is `camera.orbit` with `autoRotate` at 0.12 rad/s, positioned so the whole 75-unit-radius forest is in view. The engine owns the render loop. I added a separate `requestAnimationFrame` loop that sets `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true` on its third tick, after `app.ready()`. That is a few frames after the first one, not on the exact first frame.
